intro: Inclusive care means every LGBTQ+ person receives dignified, respectful support shaped around who they truly are, led by the person.
points: Never out anyone: a person's identity is theirs to share, so only disclose it with their clear consent.
The Equality Act 2010 protects sexual orientation and gender reassignment; trans people are protected without surgery or a certificate.
Always use the name and pronouns a person tells you are theirs; repeatedly getting them wrong deliberately can be harassment.
Make no assumptions about anyone's orientation or gender; keep an open mind and let people tell you who they are.
If you hear a discriminatory remark, challenge it calmly, support anyone affected, and report it to your manager.
Respect chosen family and never let your own beliefs affect care; speak to your manager if you feel a tension.
